stories.title: New trial of AI phone assistant to monitor patients with long-term illness
stories.synopsis: An AI assistant that holds natural, spoken phone conversations with patients is being trialed in the NHS to help clinicians keep track of people with long-term illness. To keep it from sounding robotic, linguistics experts first studied how human clinicians show empathy. Taking part is voluntary, and the AI calls are in addition to patients' regular NHS care, not a replacement for it.

stories.title: From biology to astrophysics, AI expands the boundaries of discovery
stories.synopsis: Stanford researchers are using AI to help scientists model human cells and decode the universe, across nearly every field. One team is building a foundation model that can simulate human cells to speed up drug discovery and personalized treatment. Another project, Biomni, is an AI co-scientist meant to take the tedious legwork out of biomedical research.

stories.title: How AI can support older adults without taking over care
stories.synopsis: AI can help older adults live safely and independently while keeping people at the center of their care. In the examples described, a home system alerts a community caregiver when someone's behaviour changes, and the caregiver decides how to respond. A tool called PainChek makes pain easier to recognise, while caregivers and health professionals stay in charge of what happens next.
